headline: Still no run since the trail block — absorption has now run longer than any easy reset would need. Steps hold high as a permanent background load. The first structured session remains untaken.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days

sections.overview: The picture is unchanged in its essentials but the gap is now long enough to matter as its own signal rather than as normal post-ultra recovery. Running is fully paused, and it's been paused long enough that the "first easy run" test hasn't just been delayed — it's become the single most informative data point still outstanding. Strength has been absent even longer, so its silence is now baseline rather than block-related. What's genuinely notable is that steps haven't dropped at all despite structured work being off entirely — rest-day step counts sit nearly as high as overall averages, which means the body isn't actually idle even without logged sessions. The recent four-week block that preceded this pause was enormous relative to the prior four weeks, so a stretch of low structured load is well-earned and doesn't read as regression. But absorption after even a very hard trail block has a natural length, and this is now past it.
sections.trends: The year-to-date shape is unambiguous — cumulative distance is running far ahead of the same point last year, which reflects real accumulated base, not a spike. The recent four-week jump versus the prior four weeks captures the trail block itself and shouldn't be read as a sustainable weekly trajectory; it's a discrete durability event within a longer arc. The current flat stretch is the natural trough after that event. This shape makes sense for a year-round hybrid athlete: a large durability block, then a genuine absorption dip, with the expectation that structured load returns before the dip itself becomes the trend. That return is the thing to watch, and it hasn't happened yet.
sections.threshold: Threshold pace and the associated heart rate haven't moved — the reference point is unchanged and now several weeks old. The trail block was run almost entirely at controlled, low-aerobic effort, so nothing in it would have tested or updated the top end. That means current threshold fitness is essentially an inference from an old reading plus a large volume of easy work, not a fresh measurement. It's most likely intact given the base underneath it, but it's genuinely untested, and the longer the pause runs without any faster work, the wider that uncertainty gets.
sections.zones: The recent per-session shapes are uniform: every trail run sat almost entirely in the lowest zone, with only trivial excursions higher on the longest days. That's exactly right for ultra-distance durability work and confirms the block was paced with discipline. But it also means the entire recent training signal is one-dimensional — no session has touched Z4 or Z5 in a long time. For a hybrid athlete whose identity includes speed and explosive capacity, that top-end absence is the standing gap. It's not a problem inside a durability block; it becomes one only if easy running resumes and the fast end stays untouched for even longer.
sections.hr_comparison: The strength HR entries, all from the estimated stream, sit where you'd expect for functional work — moderate averages with occasional higher-zone spikes on the more intense sessions. Nothing in the run HR data suggests any disagreement worth flagging; the trail sessions' low averages and controlled maxes are internally consistent with the paces run. No meaningful anomaly across sources.
sections.calendar: The calendar tells the clearest story: a dense, back-to-back cluster of large sessions, then an abrupt, complete stop with nothing logged since. That's a sharp binary — heavy block, then nothing — rather than a gradual taper into easy maintenance. For an athlete who normally holds a running rhythm of several sessions a week, a stretch this long with zero logged structured work is a real break in pattern, not a light week. The step data confirms movement continues underneath it, but structured training has genuinely stopped.
sections.personal_bests: None of the current bests are within reach right now, and none should be — they were set at short and middle distances that the recent block did nothing to prepare, and the training focus lately has been the opposite end entirely. When faster work does return, the short-distance PBs are the natural place to check whether the top end held through the durability phase, but that's a question for after running resumes, not now.

watch_items: Watch whether the first logged run finally appears, and whether it returns at a normal easy HR — that remains the single outstanding test of whether the block absorbed cleanly.
Watch whether the gap since the last run tips from earned absorption into an unplanned layoff — the length now matters more than the reason.
Watch whether strength re-enters at all when running resumes, or whether both remain paused together.
Watch whether the persistently high background step load is quietly substituting for structured easy volume during this pause.
